claim: Most personal computing devices have no moving parts.
originalWording: Most personal computing devices have no moving parts.

sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 6, printed p. 15

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: The pocket/worn personal computers in the surrounding passage generally use electronic storage rather than rotating media.
reference.rationale: Flash-based phones and small music players fit the devices described in the passage by 2009. This remains a full success for that device class. Buttons, haptic motors and exceptions do not defeat “for the most part.”

evidence.title: Apple: Small clip-on iPod shuffle
evidence.note: Primary institutional, research, or issuer source. Dates in the claim refer to the observation or product event, not the review date.. Primary institutional, research, or issuer source. Dates in the claim refer to the observation or product event, not the review date.

evidence.title: iPhone App Store downloads top 10 million
evidence.note: Opening announcement and descriptions of wireless application downloads and Multi-Touch features. The release establishes downloadable applications on iPhone/iPod touch and their touch interface. Evidence limits: It does not establish storage technology or the absence of moving components; see the added flash-player source.

evidence.title: Apple introduces iPod shuffle (2005)
evidence.note: USB flash-drive paragraph and Pricing & Availability section. Apple documents a shipping flash-storage player in January 2005. Interpreting flash storage as avoiding mechanical disk storage supports the portable-device criterion. Evidence limits: This is an editorial inference about storage; physical switches remain, and the source does not establish a majority across all personal devices.

strict.criterion: Apply the solid-state/no-moving-parts claim to portable PCs including laptops, not just the pocket/worn context.
strict.rationale: Hard drives were common in 2009 laptops; current widespread SSDs fulfill storage substitution, but a literal no-moving-parts condition still conflicts with many cooling fans.
